# runner

run your server's tasks on this machine

Run your Coder server's tasks on your own machine, reached through any tunnel.

## `runner add <kind> [--name <name>] [--scope <scope>] [--field <field>] [--server <server>] [--yes] [--json]`

connect a runner

Connect a runner. Secret fields read environment variables with key=env:VARIABLE. Adding local prints a pairing command.

- `<kind>` the runner kind, such as local or http
- `--name <name>` runner display name
- `--scope <scope>` personal or workspace
- `--field <field>` repeat for each field, use env:VARIABLE for secrets
- `--server <server>` act on your Coder server, in the saved workspace
- `--yes` connect to a server used for the first time without asking
- `--json` JSON output

## `runner default <id> [--server <server>] [--yes] [--json]`

set the default in its scope

Use this runner by default within its scope.

- `<id>` the runner
- `--server <server>` act on your Coder server, in the saved workspace
- `--yes` connect to a server used for the first time without asking
- `--json` JSON output

## `runner serve [--url <url>] [--token <token>] [--runner-url <runner-url>] [--port <port>] [--name <name>] [--workspace] [--server <server>] [--yes] [--json] [--cwd <cwd>]`

run your server's tasks on this machine

Run tasks on this machine with its own claude and codex logins. Expose the port with any tunnel (cloudflared, ngrok, Tailscale Funnel or a public VS Code port) and pass the tunnel's URL; each start registers the current URL, so a changing tunnel URL is fine. Choose a default with coder runner default. Tasks use their named runner, the agent setting, your default, the workspace default, then the server default.

- `--url <url>` the HTTPS address the server reaches this runner at
- `--token <token>` one-use pairing token, --url is the Coder server
- `--runner-url <runner-url>` public tunnel address when pairing, or CODER_RUNNER_URL
- `--port <port>` local port the tunnel forwards to (default 4100)
- `--name <name>` shown in the dashboard (default: this machine's hostname)
- `--workspace` run every member's tasks, not only yours (owners and admins)
- `--server <server>` act on your Coder server, in the saved workspace
- `--yes` connect to a server used for the first time without asking
- `--json` JSON output
- `--cwd <cwd>` workspace directory (default: current)

```sh
cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:4100  # expose the port in one terminal
coder runner serve --url https://abc.trycloudflare.com  # then serve through it
```
